finding.title: Replace vacuous isNotNull/isNotEmpty assertions in user_database_managers_refs_test.dart with relationship-verifying checks
finding.why: 41 of the file's 42 tests (every test except 'filter by displayName' at line 175-183) assert only isNotNull on a getter whose return type is non-nullable ($$XTableProcessedTableManager, confirmed by grepping user_database.g.dart — never `?`), or isNotEmpty on rows that come from the base table regardless of the specific ref/prefetch-flag/computedField under test. Verified line 23 (`import 'package:drift/drift.dart' hide isNotNull, isNull;`) confirms these are flutter_test's boolean matchers, not SQL builders. Concretely: deleting `curriculumScopesRefs: true` from the prefetch call at line 374, or breaking the FK the getter filters on in user_database.dart, would not fail any of these tests — the isNotNull can only fail via an exception (impossible given the type), and isNotEmpty is satisfied by the parent row alone. The file's own header claims this suite 'covers' the References/prefetch classes; it cannot detect a broken relationship or prefetch join.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite assertions to depend on the specific thing under test: e.g. call `.get()` on the returned manager and assert the rows' FK column equals the parent id used in setUp, or assert a real row count/field value through the prefetched cache, or compare a flag-on vs flag-off query to show the flag changed behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each affected test fails if the specific relationship/prefetch flag it names is broken or removed (verify by temporarily deleting one `xxxRefs: true` flag or its underlying FK reference and confirming exactly the corresponding test — not an unrelated one — turns red).
No automated checker exists for this class of test-rigor defect; acceptance is code-review confirmation the assertion depends on the parameter under test.

finding.title: Stop TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl importing ContentRepository directly — compose in a service/notifier (SM-8)
finding.why: TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl takes a ContentRepository constructor dependency and calls `_contentRepository.getContentForCurriculum(...)` directly from three of its own methods (_buildSedarimIndex, _buildMasechtosIndex). This is exactly the repository-imports-repository shape SM-8 forbids: unit-testing this repository now requires faking or booting ContentRepository's dependency chain instead of a clean seam, and the file's own doc comments on MasechtaOrderingPolicy already flag this as a known-wrong coupling ('Unblocks W4.22 (_buildMasechtosIndex removal from the repository impl)') that the team is mid-way through unwinding.
finding.recommendation: Move the content-fetch + index-build orchestration into a domain service or the notifier that currently constructs TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl, passing the already-resolved content list/indices into the repository (or into MasechtaOrderingPolicy directly), so the repository itself only talks to its own DAO.
acceptance_criteria: TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl no longer imports anything under features/content_browsing/.
A unit test constructs TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl with only a fake/in-memory database (no ContentRepository fake required).
SM-8's grep/lint (once implemented) reports zero repository→repository imports in lib/features/tracks/.

finding.title: Merge duplicate LearningProgramRepository test suites (learning_program_repository_test.dart + learning_program_service_test.dart)
finding.rule: Fowler duplication lens + TQ-1 (pyramid/test-suite hygiene, avoid redundant suites)

evidence.quote: test('programs have sequential ids starting at 1', () {
test('program ids are sequential starting from 1', () {

finding.why: Both files exist purely to test LearningProgramRepository (a ~60-line class) via LearningProgramRepository.instance, and both independently cover getAllPrograms, getActivePrograms, getProgramById (valid/0/out-of-range), getProgramByName (found/missing) and getProgramsByCurriculumType/getActiveProgramsByCurriculumType with near-identical assertions restated in different words. 329 combined lines maintain one class's coverage in two places that can silently drift — one file hardcodes 'daf_yomi'/'bavli' fixture literals the other lacks — and a reviewer who finds only one of the two would reasonably (and wrongly) believe it is the sole coverage. This is the concrete cost the AG-5 mispathing finding predicted: because neither test sits at the discoverable mirrored path, whoever wrote the second file evidently didn't find the first.
finding.recommendation: Merge into a single file at the mirrored path test/features/scheduler/domain/services/learning_program_service_test.dart, keeping the union of unique cases (the daf_yomi/bavli literal checks, testConfig/displayName field checks) and dropping exact duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one test file covers LearningProgramRepository, at the mirrored path
flutter test green; no unique assertion from either original file is lost

It is the ONLY test in the repo for optimistic_completion_provider.dart (verified: no other test file references optimisticCompletionStateProvider or optimisticKey), so its coverage is real, but AG-5's mirrored-path convention would lead anyone looking for that provider's test to test/features/learning/presentation/providers/optimistic_completion_provider_test.dart and find nothing. finding.title: Tighten st3_settings_switch_a11y_test.dart to assert the Hebrew-Terms Switch specifically, not any labelled Switch
finding.rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong)
finding.why: S1's assertion loops every `Switch` widget found in SettingsScreen and passes as soon as ANY of them has a non-empty semantics label — it never isolates the Hebrew-Terms tile's own Switch. Today settings_screen.dart has exactly one bare `Switch(` (confirmed by grep), so the test is currently equivalent to the intended check, but that equivalence is accidental, not encoded. A second labelled Switch added anywhere else on the (816-line, HOTSPOT) SettingsScreen in a future change would make this ST-3 regression guard keep passing even if `_HebrewTermsTile`'s own `Semantics(label: ...)` wrapper were removed or broken.
finding.recommendation: Locate the Switch that is a descendant of the PreferenceListTile carrying l10n.hebrewTermsPreference (or add a Key to _HebrewTermsTile's Switch) and assert that specific Switch's semantics label contains/equals l10n.hebrewTermsPreference, not 'any switch in the screen has a label'.
acceptance_criteria: The test fails if a second, unrelated, labelled Switch is added to SettingsScreen while _HebrewTermsTile's Semantics wrapper is removed.
